{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nv-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7e96a30d32e5a32caf38fb691d9beff7e8f9f5c8e1f021a7f714832a172947c2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","source_liveness_sha256":"0dfbf3aa4b4798b88d69252e076642b5f0a38751c5010711fbce93c8a7d6e292"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Defensive driving, phones, roundabouts, signals and turns, U-turns, passing and parking","heading":"C — Defensive driving and following distance, phone use, police stops, roundabouts, hand signals and turns, lane changes, U-turns, passing, cyclists, parking, curb colors and no-parking zones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Defensive driving and following distance, phone use, police stops, roundabouts, hand signals and turns, lane changes, U-turns, passing, cyclists, parking, curb colors and no-parking zones
Knowledge domain: how far to look ahead and how far to follow, what Nevada allows with a phone, how to drive a roundabout, how to signal, turn, change lanes and make a U-turn legally, when passing is and is not allowed, and how and where to park.

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Look ahead at least 12 seconds, to the spot your vehicle will reach 12 seconds from now; at 30 mph that is a little more than one block. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
If you drive 40 mph or less, keep at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead; that is only the minimum, and most driving instructors recommend up to four seconds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Stopping from 55 mph takes almost seven seconds even with perfect brakes and ideal roads, so leave more room at highway speeds and whenever roads are slippery or visibility is poor. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Just before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A02
Holding a cell phone or other handheld wireless device for a voice call while driving is prohibited unless you use a hands-free accessory. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A02
Using a handheld device by hand to text, send or read messages, search the Internet or otherwise communicate without voice is prohibited while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A02
You may use a handheld device to report an emergency when stopping the vehicle would be inadvisable, impractical or dangerous. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
If police lights flash behind you, pull over as far out of the traffic lane as you can, stay inside the vehicle, and at night switch on the interior light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A02
During a police stop, keep your hands where the officer can see them, ideally on the steering wheel, avoid sudden movements, and wait to be asked for your license, registration and proof of insurance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A03
Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to the traffic already circulating in it, and all traffic travels around it counterclockwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A03
In a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane to turn left, make a U-turn or go straight, and the right lane to turn right or go straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A03
Inside a roundabout, slow to the speed of the traffic already circulating, and switch on your right turn signal as you exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A04
Signalling before you turn, change lanes, slow down, stop or park is required by law, not just a courtesy. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A04
Hand signals: a left arm held straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at about a right angle means a right turn, and a left arm pointed down with the palm facing back means slowing or stopping. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A04
On city streets, turn your signal on no less than 100 feet (roughly 10 car lengths) before the turn; on open highways make it 300 feet (roughly 30 car lengths). [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A04
For a right turn, be in the far right travel lane or a lane marked for right turns; a lane reserved for right turns may be entered only to turn right, never to drive straight through. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A04
For a left turn, keep the wheels pointed straight until you actually start turning, and on a two-way road turn from the lane just right of the center line into the nearest lane going your way. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A05
To change lanes, check the rear and side mirrors, signal at least 100 feet ahead in the city or 300 feet on highways and freeways, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, and never change lanes inside an intersection. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A05
U-turns are generally legal on any Nevada road where they can be made safely; signal and make them from the far left lane or the center left-turn lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A05
A U-turn is legal across a double yellow line when safe and legal, at an intersection on a green light or green arrow unless a No U-turn sign is posted, and on a divided highway only through an opening in the divider. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A05
U-turns are illegal on or at railroad tracks, on a one-way street, where a No U-turn sign is posted, or where other vehicles could hit you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A05
Never make a U-turn where a curve, hill, rain, fog or anything else keeps you from seeing 200 feet clearly in each direction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A05
Never make a U-turn in a business district, which also covers areas with churches, apartments, multifamily housing and public buildings; there, turn only at an intersection or a provided opening. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A05
Never make a U-turn in front of a fire station or use a fire station driveway to turn around. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A06
Never go over the speed limit to pass, and never use the road shoulder to pass. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A06
On a two-lane road with opposing traffic, pass on the left only when you can see clearly ahead with no oncoming traffic close by, the broken yellow line is on your side, and it is safe. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A06
On a two-lane road, do not pass when nearing a curve or hilltop that hides the road ahead, at or within 100 feet of a street or railroad crossing, where a double solid yellow line is painted, or where signs forbid it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A06
After passing, return to your lane once you can see the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A06
When a vehicle behind you signals to pass, move right within your lane and let it go by, and never speed up while it is passing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A06
Never pass on the left of a driver who is making or signalling a left turn. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A06
On a highway with two lanes in your direction, it is illegal to drive the far left lane below the posted limit while a faster vehicle is coming up behind you in that lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A06
You may pass on the right only where the road is clearly marked for two or more lanes going your way and it is safe, and never if it would take you off the paved road. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A07
To pass a cyclist, move into the next lane to the left if there is one going your way and it is reasonably safe; otherwise pass at a safe distance of at least three feet and do not move back right until clear. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A07
Driving in a marked bicycle lane is prohibited. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A07
When you park and leave the vehicle, turn off the engine and set the parking brake, and look for bicycles and other vehicles before opening your door. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A07
Park facing the direction normal traffic flows, with the front and rear wheels within 18 inches of the curb. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A07
Park where other drivers can see your vehicle from 200 feet away (roughly 20 car lengths) in both directions. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A07
Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is moving, because the steering will lock when you turn the wheel and you will lose control. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A07
Curb colors: white usually allows only a very short stop to load or unload passengers or drop mail, green allows parking for a limited time, yellow marks a loading zone, red means no stopping, standing or parking, and blue marks handicapped parking. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A08
When parking on a hill, aim the front tires so a rolling car moves into the curb or away from traffic: downhill toward the curb or shoulder, uphill with a curb away from it, uphill without a curb toward the shoulder, and always set the parking brake. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A09
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant where parallel parking is allowed, or within 20 feet of one where angle parking is allowed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A09
Do not park on a crosswalk or within 20 feet of one, or within 30 feet of a roadside traffic signal on a highway. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A09
Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance, or within 75 feet of that entrance on the opposite side of the highway. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A09
Parking in a space marked with the international symbol of access is allowed only when the person issued the valid disabled placard or plate is driving or riding in the vehicle, and the minimum fine for anyone else is $250. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

Misconceptions: the two-second gap is a minimum, not a target; a right-turn-only lane cannot be used to go straight; the left lane of a roundabout can also go straight; U-turns are not banned everywhere in Nevada, only in listed places; passing on the shoulder is never legal; on a hill with a curb, uphill tires point away from the curb, not toward it.
Mnemonics: twelve to look, two to follow, four to be safe; city one hundred, highway three hundred for signals; hydrant fifteen parallel, twenty angle; crosswalk twenty, signal thirty; curb colors white wait, green go-limited, yellow load, red no, blue disabled.
Glossary: following distance means the time gap between you and the vehicle ahead; roundabout means a circular intersection where traffic flows counterclockwise without signals; truck apron means the raised ring around a roundabout's center island for large trucks; blind spot means the area your mirrors do not show; business district means an area of businesses, churches, apartments or public buildings where mid-block U-turns are banned.
Dynamic facts: local authorities and the state transportation department can ban U-turns at any location, and limited-time parking periods are shown on local signs, so posted signs govern.
